ai.definition: Digital physics is a theoretical framework that models the physical universe as a computational process or a vast network of discrete elements. It explores whether the fundamental laws of nature can be described by digital information and computation.
ai.howItWorks: By representing physical phenomena using algorithms, digital physics seeks to understand how classical and quantum mechanics might emerge from underlying computational processes. This involves creating simulations that mimic real-world systems at various scales, from subatomic particles to complex macroscopic structures.
ai.problemSolved: Digital physics aims to bridge the gap between theoretical computer science and fundamental physics by providing a new perspective on the nature of reality, potentially unifying different physical theories under a computational framework.
ai.manufacturing: Not directly applicable as digital physics is primarily a theoretical field. However, it could influence future manufacturing processes through more efficient simulations and design tools.
ai.buildProcess: Involves developing complex algorithms to simulate physical systems, often using high-performance computing resources. The process includes defining the computational model, implementing it in software, and validating its accuracy against experimental data.
ai.costDrivers: High-performance computing resources, advanced algorithm development, and extensive validation processes are key cost drivers. Additionally, the complexity of models can lead to significant development time and resource requirements.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Theoretical and exploratory phase with potential for future technological advancements but not yet commercially viable.
ai.regulation: Not currently regulated as a technology; primarily governed by academic and research institutions. However, any practical applications could face regulatory scrutiny once they become more concrete.
ai.risks: Risk of theoretical divergence from empirical evidence, difficulty in validating models against real-world phenomena, and the potential for computational limitations to constrain model accuracy.
ai.profitability: Not directly profitable at this stage; primarily driven by academic and research interests. Potential for future profitability if practical applications are developed.
ai.futureDevelopment: Could lead to new technologies such as advanced simulations, quantum computing, and a deeper understanding of the universe's fundamental nature. However, significant theoretical and empirical challenges remain.

glossary.def: The hypothesis that reality is a computer simulation
Individual units or nodes in a computational model representing physical phenomena
A series of operations performed by a computer to solve problems or simulate systems

subsystems.name: Discrete substrate
subsystems.role: replaces smooth space and time with a finite set of states and an update rule.
parts: lattice, causal set or cellular-automaton rule

subsystems.name: Quantum information layer
subsystems.role: treats qubits and their entanglement — not fields — as the fundamental description.

subsystems.name: Continuum limit
subsystems.role: shows how known physics emerges when the discrete model is viewed at large scales.

subsystems.name: Holographic description
subsystems.role: writes the interior of space as encoded on a lower-dimensional boundary.

subsystems.name: Simulation stack
subsystems.role: runs the model, either approximately on classical machines or natively on quantum hardware.
parts: quantum simulators (superconducting circuits, trapped ions, neutral atoms)

subsystems.name: Falsification apparatus
subsystems.role: looks for the tiny signatures a discrete or simulated universe would leave.
parts: precision atomic clocks and atom interferometers
low-noise interferometers such as the Fermilab Holometer

buildSteps.title: Pick a discrete substrate
buildSteps.detail: Choose a finite rule set — a lattice, a causal set of discrete events, or a cellular automaton — rather than continuous spacetime.

buildSteps.title: Write an update rule with the right symmetries
buildSteps.detail: The rule must generate three-dimensional space, locality and the symmetries of the Standard Model, or it is dead on arrival.

buildSteps.title: Recover known physics in the continuum limit
buildSteps.detail: Show that at scales far above the Planck length the model reproduces quantum field theory, general relativity and the measured particle masses.

buildSteps.title: Account for gravity and black-hole entropy
buildSteps.detail: A working model must produce the observed entropy of black holes and something like the holographic bound on information in a region.

buildSteps.title: Simulate it classically
buildSteps.detail: Run small versions on supercomputers with tensor-network methods to check predictions against experiments.

buildSteps.title: Map it onto quantum hardware
buildSteps.detail: Encode the rule on a quantum simulator so systems too entangled for classical machines can be run.

buildSteps.title: Hunt for deviations
buildSteps.detail: Derive observable consequences — a minimum length, slightly different photon speeds at extreme energies, or holographic noise — and set limits with existing instruments.

buildSteps.title: Compare and discard
buildSteps.detail: Models that predict effects already ruled out are dropped; survivors are pushed to larger simulated systems and finer experiments.

prerequisites.why: simulating fundamental discrete models natively needs far more logical qubits than today's machines.
these let classical supercomputers approximate strongly entangled quantum systems today.

prerequisites.tech: A testable theory of quantum gravity
prerequisites.why: without one there is no agreed calculation that connects a discrete rule to observed physics.
observations of distant gamma-ray bursts already constrain some forms of spacetime discreteness.
it supplies the main worked examples of how geometry could emerge from entanglement.

pathway.milestone: quantum information treated as fundamental; classical simulation of toy discrete models
pathway.unlocks: concrete, checkable statements about spacetime discreteness.

pathway.milestone: larger quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories and holographic toy models
pathway.unlocks: evidence for or against specific discrete rules.

pathway.milestone: a quantum-gravity framework that predicts a measurable deviation
pathway.unlocks: a real experiment rather than a thought experiment.

pathway.milestone: dedicated precision experiments reaching Planck-scale sensitivity
pathway.unlocks: either a detection of discreteness or durable limits that rule whole families of models out.
